SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 
 
August 14, 2026 
 
A Special Meeting of the Council of the City of Vancouver was held on Friday, August 14, 2026, 
at 8:28 am, in the Council Chamber, Third Floor, City Hall, for the purpose of considering the 
motion entitled “Public Safety Plebiscite.” This Special Council meeting was convened in person 
and via electronic means as authorized by Part 14 of the Procedure By-law. 
 
PRESENT: 
Mayor Ken Sim 
Acting Mayor Lenny Zhou 
Councillor Rebecca Bligh* 
Councillor Lisa Dominato 
Councillor Pete Fry* 
Councillor Sarah Kirby-Yung 
Councillor Mike Klassen 
Councillor Lucy Maloney 
Councillor Peter Meiszner 
Councillor Brian Montague 
Councillor Sean Orr* 
 
 
CITY MANAGER’S OFFICE: 
Donny van Dyk, City Manager 
Sandra Singh, Deputy City Manager 
 
CITY CLERK’S OFFICE: 
Andrew Aguilar, Deputy City Clerk 
David Yim, Meeting Coordinator 
* Denotes absence for a portion of the meeting.  
 
 
WELCOME 
 
The Mayor acknowledged we are on the unceded homelands of the Musqueam, Squamish, and 
Tsleil-Waututh People. We thank them for having cared for this land and look forward to working 
with them in partnership as we continue to build this great city together. 
 
The Mayor also recognized the immense contributions of the City of Vancouver’s team 
members who work hard every day to help make our city an incredible place to live, work, and 
play. 
 
* * * * * 
 
Due to technical difficulties, the meeting recessed at 8:31 am and reconvened in the Cascadia 
Room at 9:15 am. 
 
* * * * * 
 
 
 

Special Council Meeting 
Minutes, Friday, August 14, 2026 
2 
 
 
1. 
Public Safety Plebiscite 
 
* * * * * 
 
At the beginning of the item, Mayor Sim relinquished the Chair to Acting Mayor Zhou to 
introduce the motion and to participate in debate and discussion. Mayor Sim resumed the Chair 
after the vote on the item. 
 
* * * * * 
 
MOVED by Mayor Sim 
SECONDED by Councillor Kirby-Yung 
 
THAT Council enact a By-law in the form set out in Appendix A of the motion entitled 
“Public Safety Plebiscite,” containing the questions to be submitted for the opinion of the 
electors in the municipal election to be held in October 2026. 
 
carried 
 
AMENDMENT MOVED by Councillor Maloney 
SECONDED by Councillor Bligh 
 
THAT the motion be struck and replaced with the following: 
 
A. 
THAT Council direct staff to develop, and report back by Q1 2027, on a 
crisis mitigation program modelled on Vancouver’s successful 2021-2022 
Better Together Collective Action Pilot program, funded and coordinated 
by the City, delivering:  
 
i. 
Neighborhood Collective Action Tables (‘Tables’), Agency-Led and 
Resident-Led; 
ii. 
A Peer Stewardship Program; 
iii. 
Education and Training; 
iv. 
Outreach and Coordination; and 
v. 
Neighborhood Cleanliness, Graffiti & Garbage Clean Up. 
 
B. 
THAT Council direct staff to report back on how to conduct a Crisis  
Response System Review by Q1 2027, that addresses crisis response 
roles and responsibilities of relevant organizations including but not 
limited to:  
 
i. 
Vancouver Coastal Health; 
ii. 
CMHA BC; 
iii. 
E-Comm; 
iv. 
the Vancouver Police Department and Vancouver Police Board; 
v. 
the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations; 
vi. 
urban Indigenous organizations; 
vii. 
crisis-line and 988 providers; 
viii. 
peer-led and community organizations; and 
ix. 
people with lived and living experience. 

Special Council Meeting 
Minutes, Friday, August 14, 2026 
3 
 
 
FURTHER THAT staff study and report back during the above Crisis 
Response System Review on how to design and roll out a Crisis 
Response, Community Led (CRCL) expansion program. 
 
C. 
THAT Council direct staff to study and report back by Q1 2027 on how to 
fund and implement an expanded commitment to adopt the Restorative 
City Framework. 
 
D. 
THAT Council direct staff to study and report back on how to adopt a 
Housing First policy that treats supportive housing as a fundamental pillar 
of community safety and restorative justice. 
 
FURTHER THAT in developing this program, staff consult relevant 
organizations including, but not limited to: 
 
i. 
Vancouver BIAs; 
ii. 
Vancouver Coastal Health; 
iii. 
Providence Healthcare; 
iv. 
Vancouver Aboriginal Child and Family Services Society; 
v. 
The Indigenous Crisis Response Team; 
vi. 
The Coordinated Community Response Network; 
vii. 
Hogan’s Alley Society; and 
viii. 
The Vancouver Police Department. 
 
LOST (Vote No. 11939) 
(Councillors Dominato, Kirby-Yung, Klassen, Meiszner, Montague, Zhou, and Mayor Sim 
opposed) 
(Councillors Bligh, Fry and Orr abstained from the vote) 
 
 
* * * * * 
 
At 9:58 am, Councillor Kirby-Yung rose on a point of order under Section 8.7 of the Procedure 
By-law, noting that Councillor Bligh’s comment was not related to the matter under discussion. 
After consulting with staff, the Chair ruled on the point of order and found it not in order but 
noted the rule of conduct set out in Section 6.1(b) of the Procedure By-law. 
 
* * * * * 
 
The amendment having lost, the motion was put and CARRIED (Vote No. 11940) with 
Councillor Maloney opposed and Councillors Bligh, Fry and Orr absent for the vote. 
 
 
ADJOURNMENT 
 
MOVED by Councillor Klassen 
SECONDED by Councillor Dominato 
 
THAT the meeting be adjourned. 
 

Special Council Meeting 
Minutes, Friday, August 14, 2026 
4 
 
 
CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 
(Councillors Bligh, Fry and Orr absent for the vote) 
 
 
The Special Council adjourned at 10:25 am. 
 
 
* * * * *

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Public Safety Plebiscite motion
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver City Council will consider a motion at its August 14, 2026 Special Council meeting to enact a by-law placing two public safety questions on the October 2026 municipal election ballot. The questions ask voters whether the city should strengthen laws to forbid open-air hard drug (Heroin, Meth, Fentanyl, Crack) use in public spaces, and whether the city should ask the Province to convert portions of the old St. Paul's Hospital into a secure medical facility with voluntary and 100-plus involuntary care beds for severe substance use and mental health disorders.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for council's decision at the August 14, 2026 meeting — approval would put these questions on the October 2026 ballot.

minutes_briefs.title: Council approved by-law for Public Safety Plebiscite questions
minutes_briefs.summary: Vancouver City Council voted to enact a by-law that sets the questions for the Public Safety Plebiscite. These questions will be put to voters in the October 2026 municipal election. The by-law was passed as presented in the motion, meaning the exact wording of the questions is now official. This decision finalizes what will appear on the ballot for the public to weigh in on public safety matters.
minutes_briefs.action_required: No immediate action needed, but stay informed about the plebiscite questions ahead of the October 2026 election.

minutes_briefs.title: Council defeats crisis mitigation program amendment
minutes_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council voted down an amendment that would have replaced a motion with a new crisis mitigation program. The defeated plan would have directed staff to develop a program modeled on the 2021-2022 Better Together Collective Action Pilot, including neighborhood action tables, a peer stewardship program, and graffiti cleanup. It also would have ordered studies on a crisis response system review, a Restorative City Framework, and a Housing First policy. The amendment was lost, with seven councillors and the mayor opposed, and three councillors abstaining.
